column1: # What a comparison returns. Registering this kind is what turns
# `1000 MB = 1 GB` from an unresolvable expression into `true`.
# `true` and `false` are not translated, and that is this file's finding
# rather than an oversight it hides: the kind ships no vocabulary at all,
# so `formatValue` degrades to the unit key in every language. A German
# engine answering "true" is what the code does today, and a row asserting
# it is what makes a later `boolean/locale/de` a visible diff here.
# The decimal comma and the group dot, German's pair and English's read
# backwards: "1,5" is three halves here and "1.500" is fifteen hundred.
# The number axis German mostly does not have. "Meter" is invariant after a
# numeral; "Meile" is the one length unit whose plural is marked.
# The dative the conversion preposition governs, read on the way in — and
# "nach" beside "in" as a second way to spell the target.
# `compoundSplitter` on a right-headed compound the lexer cannot cut and no
# The word operators. "mal" stands alone; "geteilt durch" is two tokens
# `in` is the conversion keyword, so the inch is typed "Zoll" and never "in".
# Every German noun is capitalised in prose and bare in a search box, and
# both spellings have to reach the same unit.
